'''''Rumex longifolius''''', commonly known as the '''dooryard dock'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=RULO2|taxon=Rumex longifolius|accessdate=26 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Lee |editor1-first=Sangtae |editor2-last=Chang |editor2-first=Kae Sun |title=English Names for Korean Native Plants |year=2015 |publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]] |location=Pocheon |isbn=978-89-97450-98-5 |page=614 |url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |accessdate=15 March 2019 |via=[[Korea Forest Service]]}}</ref> or '''northern dock''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a perennial species of plant in the genus ''[[Rumex]]''.

A [[variety (botany)|variety]] has been described:
* ''Rumex longifolius'' var. ''nanus''

==Description==
[[File:Hevonhierakka.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Rumex longifolius''.]]
''Rumex longifolius'' is a perennial plant that grows to a height of {{convert|60|to|120|cm|0|abbr=on}}. It has large, broad leaves, the edges of which are crinkled and undulating. The upper surface of the leaves is hairless and the under surface hairy beside the veins. The stems are erect, tough, and unbranched until just below the [[inflorescence]]. The junctions of the stems are covered by two fused stipules which form an [[ochrea]], a thin, paper-like sheath - a characteristic of the family [[Polygonaceae]], and fringed above in this species. The stem leaves are alternate and are narrowly ovate–lanceolate and have a rounded or tapered base. The leaf stalks are approximately the same length as the leaf blade. The inflorescence consists of large clusters of [[raceme]]s which contain small greenish [[flower]]s that are bisexual. The perianth-segments are in two whorls of three. Segments in the outer whorl are small and spreading while the inner whorl forms the fruit valves, which are rounded or kidney-shaped and have either entire edges or crinkly ones. Each flower has six stamens, a pistil consisting of three fused carpels and three styles. The fruit is a glossy brown nut with a triangular cross section. This plant blooms from July to September.<ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/northern-dock |title=Northern Dock: ''Rumex longifolius'' |publisher=NatureGate |accessdate=2013-12-30}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Rumex longifolius'' is native to Europe, including Britain, from Scandinavia southwards and eastwards to the Pyrenees, the Caucasus, Western and Central Asia. It chiefly grows in open areas such as on roadsides, in arable fields and in damp grassy places.<ref name=NatureGate/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Rumex+longifolius |title=''Rumex longifolius'' |publisher=Plants For A Future |accessdate=2013-12-30}}</ref>
